1.explanation: All of the F# syntax rules—including comment delimiters—are defined inside the exported function in fsharp.js. The call to hljs.COMMENT('\\(\\*','\\*\\)') registers "(* ... *)" as the F# multiline comment delimiters. Because Operators.(*) contains the exact sequence "(*", the highlighter treats it as the start of a comment. To fix this, you need to adjust or reorder the comment rule (or add an exception) within the exported function so that Operators.(*) and similar operator calls are not interpreted as comment delimiters.
1.bug_scenario: In the F# code snippet the call to Operators.(*) is being picked up as the start of a multiline comment ("(*"), so the rest of the code block is highlighted as if it were inside a comment. In the screenshot you can see that everything after the line with Operators.(*) is greyed out as though it were part of a comment, even though it isn’t.

2.explanation: The root of the highlighting bug is in src/languages/fsharp.js, inside the main exported function that defines the F# grammar. In its contains list it invokes hljs.COMMENT('\\(\\*','\\*\\)') to detect F# multi-line comments. Because it simply looks for any literal "(*" and "*)", an operator call written as "(*)" is incorrectly recognized as the start and end of a comment delimiter. This means that Operators.(*) will be treated as a comment, and everything that follows is swallowed as comment text. To fix the issue, the comment rule or its placement/order in the grammar must be refined so that it does not trigger on operator usage patterns like Operators.(*) without a real comment context.
2.bug_scenario: In an F# code snippet posted in Discord’s syntax-highlighted code block, using the Operators.(*) function triggers the F# multi-line comment rule (which begins on "(*" and ends on "*)"). The highlighter mistakes the operator call "(*)" for the start of a comment, causing the rest of the code block to be rendered as a comment.
